investigation: AnthemScore online installer and declared repository payload: static component/model/viewer analysis

identity.installer_framework_version: 4.8.1.0 (PE fixed-version data; not the AnthemScore application version)

questions.question: What is the supplied EXE?
questions.answer: An x64 native Qt Installer Framework online bootstrapper. The appended QResource configuration selects the AnthemScore repository and installs to @ApplicationsDirX64@/AnthemScore. It is not a self-contained copy of the music application.

questions.question: Which actual application was inspected?
questions.answer: The live repository explicitly declared by the bootstrapper served package 6.3.100, release date 2026-09-30. Its AnthemScore.exe reports file/product version 6.3.0.0. Package metadata and content/resources were downloaded, hashed and extracted without running them.
questions.limitation: This is the live repository payload at retrieval time, not application code embedded in the original installer. Repository and PE version numbers identify different layers.

questions.question: What components are used?
questions.answer: Native x64 C++/Qt 6 desktop app; Qt Multimedia and packaged FFmpeg audio libraries; packaged ONNX Runtime and embedded ONNX models; MusicXML generation; a Qt WebEngine viewer carrying OpenSheetMusicDisplay; Qt PrintSupport/WebEngine PDF printing; FluidLite and a General MIDI soundfont for synthesized playback.
questions.limitation: Imports, assets, model contracts and literals establish static references. Native orchestration and live file/network behavior were not traced.

questions.question: How are musical notes and timing found?
questions.answer: Six distinct length-prefixed ONNX ModelProto graphs were decoded from the executable. Their contracts include onset, beat/downbeat, chord/bass, instrument/percussion and volume predictions. Native labels also identify a hand tagger. Spectrogram/MultiQ/FFT references indicate spectral preprocessing. RhythmQuantize diagnostics reference beat repair, swing, triplets and rolled notes.
questions.limitation: The precise preprocessing parameters, model-selection logic, thresholds, full data flow, training data and recognition accuracy are not established.

questions.question: How does recognition become printable sheet music?
questions.answer: The native image contains MusicXML score-partwise templates and exports. Its packaged HTML sets xmlInputFile to a generated MusicXML path and loads OpenSheetMusicDisplay. The JavaScript contains XML load/render logic and PDF/MIDI/MusicXML export actions. Native imports include QWebEnginePage::printToPdf. Static evidence supports MusicXML -> browser-based engraving/viewing -> PDF.
questions.limitation: No score was rendered or exported. REA viewer semantics remain partial after a heap-budget exhaustion; manually inspected snippets and declared imports provide the bounded evidence.

questions.question: What matters for full mixed songs?
questions.answer: The app has explicit auto instrument detection and percussion detection. Its help text states that instrument detection assigns notes to their played instrument; when unchecked all notes are written to piano. The percussion tooltip specifically mentions drum and cymbal hits. The trial message states a 30-second limit.
questions.limitation: The state of the checkbox by default, exact edition entitlements, recognition quality, and runtime enforcement were not tested.

package_acquisition.checks: Metadata archive SHA-1 matched Updates.xml. Core/resource archive SHA-1 values matched their published sidecars. 7-Zip extraction completed successfully. Absolute paths, traversal and link entries were rejected before extraction.

rea_evidence.coverage: Partial: selected minified source exceeded 512 MiB analysis heap; no complete viewer semantic graph was established.

limitations: The supplied installer, application, native DLLs, JavaScript viewer and models were not executed. No installation or benchmark was performed.

The actual app was acquired from the repository URL embedded in the supplied bootstrapper. Live repository contents can change; URLs, response headers, timestamps, archive hashes and executable identity were retained.
Qt framework/translation dependency archives were not downloaded because they were not needed for static component inspection. The extracted payload is not claimed to be a runnable installation.
No native function-level decompilation was available. Spectral preprocessing, orchestration and model role mapping remain partly inferred from declared contracts, names, imports and help strings.

The REA JavaScript worker exhausted its explicitly bounded 512 MiB heap on the minified bundle. Partial Evidence is retained in viewer-evidence.bundle.json; no retry or complete semantic graph is claimed.
Model tensor shapes are graph interfaces, not verified user-facing limits on instrument counts or musical range.
Embedded English resources include older/shared licensing messages. Only the explicit 30-second trial message is reported; exact trial and edition behavior was not tested.
No guarantee of perfect instrument separation, faithful reconstruction of all parts, or absence of network activity can be derived from this static inspection.
